thesis: The bear carries the argument against an immediate add because a quarterly recovery and small bounce do not establish a sustained, adequately priced turnaround. Nearly flat H1 earnings,122-day-old credit evidence and weak-volume stabilization favor waiting. This is not an automatic liquidation verdict on an existing recovery exposure.
strongest_counterexample: Q2 attributable profit rose9.8%, with reported capital17.8% and impaired financing0.98%; those facts preserve a credible recovery scenario despite weak timing evidence.
invalidation_conditions: Two subsequent comparable quarters with attributable-profit growth above0% and impaired financing at or below the observed0.98% would undermine the unconfirmed-recovery basis for waiting.
A subsequent report with attributable-profit growth below0% and impaired financing above0.98% would weaken the stable-credit recovery scenario and require a more adverse assessment.
evidence_gaps: Post-June30 funding-margin, asset-quality and capital observations.
decisive_factors: Q2 profit rose9.8% but H1 profit was nearly flat.
Capital17.8% and impaired financing0.98% are June30 observations.
Industrial FCF is not an appropriate independent bank-distress test.
